writeup.headline: Applied Optoelectronics rates Hold as explosive revenue growth is offset by losses, heavy dilution and a broken trend.
writeup.thesis: AAOI scores 53, a Hold, with growth carrying the score: latest-quarter revenue growth of 86.4% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 61.9%, and growth sped up by 35.1 pp from the previous quarter, earning a growth score of 100. Quality pulls it down at 28, with a gross margin of 28.9%, an operating margin of -11.3% and diluted share count up 43.7% year on year. The trend score of 25 reflects a sharp reversal: price 63.1% below its 52-week high and 27.7% below its 200-day average, and shares 55.3 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, even though shares are up 170.5% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. News is neutral at 50, with the August Q3 outlook of $255 million to $290 million revenue still standing ahead of results scheduled for November 5. Balance sheet and valuation were not scored, but P/S of 11.7 is high in absolute terms and more expensive than at 55 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: Still loss-making at the operating level (operating margin of -11.3%), so growth has not yet turned into profit.
Heavy dilution: diluted share count up 43.7% year on year.
Share price momentum has broken down, with price 63.1% below its 52-week high.
Dependence on a large hyperscale 1.6T order leaves the business exposed to a few big customers.
P/S of 11.7 is high in absolute terms and expensive against its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable).
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 12 more points, most plausibly from quality improving as margins turn positive and dilution slows, or from the trend score recovering.
A drop to Sell would follow a 9-point decline, for example if Q3 results on November 5 miss the $255 million to $290 million outlook and growth slows sharply.
Positive guidance or customer news could lift the news risk score above its neutral 50, while negative news would push it down.
